title: Enter the lane, start on purpose and learn the training roles
stage_label: Separate instructional exemplar · individually authored · written athletic design reviewed
status_note: This is the first separate instructional offering, not Day1 of the continuing main block. The written athletic prescription has passed scoped preparation, timing and programming review; current library/facility verification remains open. The precise separate tumbling plan is still missing.
brief: Teach the start/stop and group-flow contract while identifying eligible acceleration and basic full-body strength variations. Familiar or directly demonstrated competence can bypass instruction; unqualified behaviors receive focused coaching within time. The aim is a usable participation record, not fatigue or automatic graduation.
quality_target: Wait for release, use the correct route and gradual finish, respond to stop cues, handle equipment as instructed, and repeat comfortable selected movement patterns. Record which behaviors are repeatable and which still need prompting. No athlete is assumed to pass every domain today.
continuity: Direct intake/existing competence, with unknown evidence left unknown →OR-01 actual observed behavior and selected doses →OR-04/05 relevant conduct/running/upper-body opportunities and OR-10 next ACC/knee comparison. Completing this plan is not a requirement to attend every OR day or restart an established main athlete.
audience: 15 instructional athletes across9–11,12–14 reference and15–18; experience is independent of age. First-time participants use simple directly observed tasks. Existing skill can be demonstrated instead of retaught, and a newcomer joins the main offering current when the required domains are documented. Do not combine multiple complete OR lessons into a catch-up visit.
readiness: Check restrictions/symptoms, ability to follow basic instructions, recent/outside sport and tumbling demands. No load or speed is granted by age. Standard D is low-volume instruction, not maximal training; L further reduces physical demand. If the athlete is distressed, symptomatic or unable to follow traffic instructions, stop/defer the affected task and follow the existing facility/professional procedure. Five offerings do not require five attendances.
equipment_space: UNVERIFIED MODEL:15 marked personal preparation spaces, three separated5m teaching lanes with15m clear gradual runoff for E1 and outside walking returns, two qualified athletic coaches. Strength uses five stable individually suitable incline surfaces, five appropriately fitting benches and five individually light dumbbells for the active five-athlete wave;15mats/personal floor spaces may stay in the preparation bays. Before class assign groups so each active station's pre-set support is suitable for its assigned athletes; if support heights must change during waves, recalculate or provide additional pre-set surfaces. No equipment quantity or geometry is inferred from taxonomy labels. The primary knee/hip lessons need no box, wall or external weight. Week 1 return-path clarification: each active lane needs its own segregated one-way outside return, with no shared merge or crossing of an active lane. Inspect adequate same-direction spacing for up to two returning athletes per path and coach sightlines over all returns. No catch-up walking or overtaking is permitted. If this layout/spacing cannot be maintained, delay releases and omit later uncompleted attempts; the listed timetable is conditional.
coaching_flow: New tasks are serialized: two coaches supervise one five-athlete active group while the remaining athletes observe a named cue or recover in their marked places. Coaches retain release authority and monitor waiting behavior. No unqualified independent circuit operates while a coach teaches another task. A supported task may be demonstrated without granting independent use; stop the rotation if the required supervision fails.
time_rules: Instruction, demonstrations, recovery, changes and water stay inside these clocks. No extra correction repetitions are hidden: use the stated bouts and record any easier substitution. If more instruction is necessary, retain the simpler task and leave the competency emerging; do not speed up the repetitions or infer a pass because the timer ended. The compact first-visit base and serialized pattern model passed written design review; actual first-visit execution remains unobserved.
preparation_note: Use the fully expanded first-visit version below, preserving recognizable order, simple qualified variants and concluding hinge/squat observations. These are preparation observations, not a full pattern-qualification battery. P1/P2 then teach a simple ready position and a walking route; the main instructional block provides further explanation and controlled practice.

exercises.name: Find a quiet ready position
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC standing-static setup only; brief teaching use pending delivery mapping
exercises.set_purpose: The single3s observation identifies a comfortable ready stance and response to a stop instruction before any traveling task.
exercises.execution: From assigned bays, join the marked waiting positions only when called. Stand in a comfortable bilateral stance, arms relaxed/ready, keep feet still for the short observation and respond to the coach's release/stop cue.
exercises.cues: Find your place; stay still; listen before moving.
exercises.errors: Leaving the queue, turning it into a race start, using an unqualified hand-supported stance or ignoring the stop cue.
exercises.rationale: This first targeted task rehearses the simplest selected start and lets the coach observe foot/trunk organization that also matters to the squat entry.
exercises.metadata: Method: direct demonstration/observation. Tenets: Balance/Coordination. Pattern: standing start/brace. Equipment: marked spaces.

exercises.competency: A first-time athlete needs only a comfortable standing base and basic response to instructions. All ages use the same one3s observation. An experienced newcomer may demonstrate it directly; a failed stop/spacing check keeps travel directly supervised rather than being marked passed.
exercises.progression: Retain a comfortable stance; simplify instructions one at a time. Stop/modify for symptoms, distress or a restriction. This check is participation observation, not clinical clearance.

exercises.name: Walk the route before using speed
exercises.mapping: OR-WALK-ROUTE:orientation procedure; no sprint exercise/profile ID claimed
exercises.set_purpose: One walk-through teaches target, gradual exit, safe return and waiting position; its purpose is traffic competence, not conditioning or acceleration output.
exercises.execution: On the coach's release, walk5m through the target, continue another5m into the gradual exit and follow the separated outside path back. Do not cross an occupied lane or turn back into an approaching athlete.
exercises.cues: Through the marker; keep going to the exit; return outside.
exercises.errors: Stopping abruptly at the target, cutting across another lane, walking back against traffic or following before clearance.
exercises.rationale: The second targeted task progressively rehearses the upcoming route at walking pace after the position check. It is not the expressly blocked moving-entry sprint profile.
exercises.metadata: Method: procedural orientation. Tenets: Coordination/Body Control. Pattern: walking/traffic control. Equipment: cones/clear routes.

exercises.competency: Every age completes one coached route if basic stop/spacing behavior is present. A competent newcomer may demonstrate it directly at the same walking dose. If it fails, retain walking instruction and withhold faster travel; failure never earns extra sprinting.
exercises.progression: Permit E1 only with a known clear route, accepted stop cue and controlled finish. Retain or simplify; do not infer speed readiness from age or a four-week calendar.
exercises.continuity: P1/direct conduct evidence →one walking orientation today →E1 controlled starts, OR-04 running-space instruction and OR-10 ACC recheck. This walk does not count as a completed sprint exposure.

exercises.name: Start and finish under control
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC / standing-static identity; lower-intent technical profile is proposed, not the source high-intent output profile
exercises.set_purpose: All selected efforts share the instructional job: reproduce the start and finish behavior with concise feedback and generous recovery. The aim is participation competence and coordinated initiation, not maximum speed.
exercises.execution: Use the observed standing-static start. On release, initiate a comfortable purposeful5m run-through and slow gradually over the15m clear runoff. Exit into the outside walking route and return to the same waiting position. Coach1 controls starts;coach2 controls runoff/return.
exercises.cues: Wait; move with control; run through then slow down; return outside.
exercises.errors: Premature release, reaching for speed, sprinting into the stopping boundary, returning through a live lane or treating another athlete as a racing opponent.
exercises.rationale: A short static start isolates route and initiation while leaving time to teach group behavior. Resisted, falling, reactive-direction and maximum-velocity tasks add prerequisites that OR-01 has not established.
exercises.metadata: Method: coach-released technical attempts with recovery. Tenets: Speed/Coordination/Balance. Physiology: movement practice, not a guaranteed speed adaptation. Pattern: short acceleration/runoff. Equipment: measured clear lanes.

exercises.competency: Reference12–14 and15–18 D receive four standard5m technical starts;9–11 receives three. Compressed D uses three for every age. L uses two in every age/booking. Use only when basic route control is observed. A competent athlete bypasses unnecessary OR instruction and uses the qualified current main route; no higher-intent or extra OR reps are automatically added for experience.
exercises.progression: Hold stance, distance and intent while cue dependence reduces. Do not advance if route/finish control is inconsistent; use the already prescribed walking orientation route at the remaining offered opportunities only if the coach records that replacement and its lower-intent distance, otherwise stop the travel task. Pain/fatigue is not treated with repeat attempts.
exercises.continuity: Direct check/P1/P2 →today's actual controlled starts →OR-10 same route with a separate knee-load decision, then OR-14/18. Main ACC entry requires documented start/runoff and other participation gates; it is not granted by these planned doses.

exercises.name: Observe the knee pattern
exercises.mapping: SQUAT-BW:tempo-bodyweight-squat authored source; current profile/release unverified
exercises.set_purpose: Practice sets share the job of producing a comfortable repeatable knee-pattern action under direct observation. Small bouts allow a cue and a later repeat without accumulating failure or fatigue.
exercises.execution: Stand with feet about shoulder width and ribs organized over the pelvis. Lower into the athlete's comfortable squat range for3s, pause gently1s and stand in1s without bouncing. No box or hand assistance is presumed.
exercises.cues: Whole foot; comfortable depth; pause softly; stand tall.
exercises.errors: Chasing someone else's depth, collapsing/bouncing, holding the breath or increasing repetitions when the cue is unclear.
exercises.rationale: The authored tempo-bodyweight squat avoids demanding fifteen different box setups for the first instruction while preserving an observable knee-pattern entry. Loaded work and a box-contact task remain separate qualified choices.
exercises.metadata: Method: observed short practice sets. Tenets: Strength/Body Control. Physiology: controlled force/range practice. Pattern: squat/brace. Regions: lower body/trunk. Equipment: clear floor bay.

exercises.competency: Every age has its written low-volume dose; initial older age adds no external load. Use comfortable range, not an assumed required depth. If independent squat participation is unqualified, keep direct guided observation; a supported/contact alternative requires its exact reviewed setup. Already mastered patterns can bypass instruction through a documented main-entry choice.
exercises.progression: Repeat the chosen range and tempo with less cue dependence; loading is considered later at OR-10 from actual competence. Reduce the range or prescribed repetitions when control is inconsistent; stop symptoms/restrictions.
exercises.continuity: Intake/direct pattern evidence →today's observed bodyweight knee bouts →OR-10 knee resistance/hold decision and OR-14/18 flow/entry checks. Do not invent prior load history.

exercises.name: Distinguish the hip hinge
exercises.set_purpose: Each short set teaches hip-back movement with soft knees and organized trunk, distinct from a deep squat. This is instruction, not a heavy hamstring session.
exercises.execution: Stand tall, cross arms at the chest, soften knees and move hips back through a small owned range while the trunk stays organized. Return smoothly to standing and reset.
exercises.cues: Soft knees; hips back; stay long; stand.
exercises.errors: Turning every repetition into a squat, forcing a deep bend, extending the neck or adding an unverified wall-touch/hand-support setup.
exercises.rationale: The actual authored bodyweight hinge supplies the necessary movement lesson with little equipment/setup. It does not falsely inherit a two-dumbbell RDL identity or loading eligibility.
exercises.metadata: Method: direct demonstration and practice. Tenets: Body Control/Strength. Physiology: movement/range control. Pattern: hinge. Regions: hip/trunk. Equipment: clear floor bay.

timing_narrative:
**Targeted180s:** P1 uses40s:15s to assigned positions,10s clear instruction, then three5s observation waves with one3s standing hold per athlete. P2 uses140s:15s demonstrate the route; five three-athlete waves start at15/35/55/75/95s. Each5m target+5m walking exit has a15s clearance budget; final return gets20s and ends by130s, leaving10s contingency. If walking/return/attention needs longer, do not overlap occupied lanes; the model requires revision.

**Standard Explosiveness:**15–20min detailed traffic/start/runoff demonstration;20–22 checks/questions and assigned queue positions. D rounds begin22/26/30/34min, with five three-athlete waves at offsets0/25/50/75/100s. Ages9–11 use only the first three rounds; reference/older use four. L uses22/30min only. Allow8s for the actual5m effort,20s including runoff clearance and40s for the separated walking return. Start intervals are4min, giving at least232s after an8s effort. The last fourth-round athlete is back by36:40.36:40–40 is feedback/readiness recording;40–45 water and equipment/strength transfer. Earlier-finished groups observe/reflect rather than run extra.

**Compressed Explosiveness:**10–15min instruction/checks,15–16 queue/readiness; D rounds16/20/24min with the same five waves and clearance/return model. L uses16/24min. Final runner is back by26:40;26:40–30 recording/feedback,30–35 water and strength transfer. Three controlled efforts are retained; the fourth standard reference/older effort is explicitly removed.

**Standard Strength:** five5min teaching blocks at45–50 knee,50–55 hinge,55–60 push,60–65 row,65–70 brace;70–75 equipment park, water and domain recording. For knee/hinge/push/brace, the first60s includes demonstration and setup. Six five-athlete waves start at offsets60/95/130/165/200/235s:groups A/B/C complete set1 then A/B/C set2. The largest standard activity is26s for four total heel taps including floor setup/exit; a35s wave leaves at least9s for change/cue. Each group's next set begins105s later, with at least79s after the largest bout. The last wave ends by261s, leaving39s for final feedback and the next-task setup. L uses only the first three waves at its stated smaller dose.

Row uses a different model because both sides take longer:60s demo/setup, then groups A/B/C at60/120/180s. Eight total reps×4s+10s side change+10s handling=52s; each60s wave leaves8s for the change. Final work ends232s, leaving68s in the5min block. L uses four total reps and finishes sooner. No second row set is prescribed.

**Compressed Strength:** five4min blocks at35–39 knee,39–43 hinge,43–47 push,47–51 row,51–55 brace. One set per athlete. For knee/hinge/push/brace allow60s demo/setup; groups A/B/C start60/105/150s. Largest26s bout ends176s, leaving64s for feedback/next-task preparation. Row retains its60/120/180s starts and52s bouts, ending232s with8s before the next block's60s demonstration/setup. More complex teaching must use a simpler qualified task or remain unresolved, not consume unallocated minutes. Verify that five-athlete handovers and actual supports fit; this is modeled arithmetic, not observed first-visit teaching success.

**Walking replacement and overlapping returns:** the existing E1 walking alternative uses its explicit 5 m target + 5 m exit, with the same 15 s active-clearance allowance as P2, followed by E1’s 40 s separated return allowance. Each lane receives one athlete every 25 s because all three lanes release in each wave. A running action occupies the active lane for 20 s; walking occupies it for 15 s. Both clear before the next release, but the prior return may still be occupied. Across mixed running/walking waves, return intervals can overlap by up to 20 s, with at most two returners per dedicated path. Full return need not finish before the next active-lane release; physically segregated paths, no merge and verified spacing are required. Same-athlete rounds are at least 240 s apart: a walking return finishes within 55 s, leaving at least 185 s before the next round; running uses 60 s, leaving 180 s. Do not accelerate return walking to meet this model. The week audit records this route and its separate walking/runoff accounting; walking never earns a running pass.
alternatives:
Prescribed alternatives are reviewable conditional routes, not verified approved-release records.

**Tabletop/heel-tap gap:** use90/90 Breathing with Reach, exact lower-leg-supported-bilateral-reach candidate only if that supported supine position/reach is comfortable. Calves and heels rest on a stable individually appropriate bench/box; no heel pull, hip lift or forced breath. All ages/all modes:one set of four comfortable breath cycles, nominal5s each (comfortable2s in/3s out, no holds), very low effort,15s quiet recovery,20s setup/exit. The substituted athlete omits heel taps. In a standard booking with any breathing substitution, use one brace bout for EVERY athlete: after60s demo/setup, groups A/B/C start60/120/180s. Each breathing bout takes40s, then15s quiet recovery in the waiting bay, leaving5s handover; the final recovery ends235s, leaving65s. Qualified heel-tap athletes perform only their first prescribed set; explicitly record removal of their second set to preserve this shared teaching schedule. In compressed bookings retain60/105/150s starts;40s breathing ends before the next group starts, and15s quiet recovery occurs in the waiting bay (last recovery ends205s). Five additional suitable leg supports or a demonstrably safe pre-staged arrangement must be available; include their setup and quantity. This changes the observation to supported position/breathing; it does not qualify moving-limb control. Do not use an unverified heel-slide as if it were source66.

workload_narrative:
The standard preparation contributes its separately counted actual tasks/contacts. P1 is one3s standing hold. P2 is one5m+5m walking route, with no sprint credit. D technical running=15m for9–11 and20m for12–14/15–18 in the standard booking;compressed D=15m each. L=10m technical travel each. These prescribed efforts are below the high-intent output task, so high-intent sprint metres are zero. Record runoff and walking return separately. A substituted walk is walking, not a completed technical run.

Standard D strength practice:2knee sets+2hinge+2push+1both-side row+2brace=9observed sets, with age-specific reps above. When any supported-breathing substitution selects the mixed-cohort standard schedule, every athlete has one brace bout: standard D becomes8 observed sets, including either one heel-tap or one breathing set. Record breathing separately from moving-limb work. Compressed D and all L routes have one set of each role=5, at their explicit repetitions. age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

competency_rule.observe: Controls both backward steps and forward return with balance and stop-cue response.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral shuffle
records.purpose: Access lateral movement with organized feet and controlled orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: This low-intent short shuffle is not reactive cutting.

records.setup: Start centered. Step-close without crossing for 1 m right and 1 m left back to start. Repeat only for the familiar dose.

stop_rules: Stop if feet collide, boundary control fails or discomfort appears.

records.name: Lateral lunge with reach
records.purpose: Access comfortable lateral hip shift and stable foot pressure.

verified_local_names: Lateral Lunge to Rotational Reach Flow
card_mapping_status.limit: The related flow includes rotation; this plain reach requires exact variant review.

records.setup: Step sideways within a 0.75 m span; shift into that hip, reach toward the thigh and return. First visit keeps hands on thigh and a shallow shift.
cues: Sit gently into the stepping hip.
Reach only with controlled trunk position.
common_errors: Chasing depth or lifting support foot unexpectedly.
stop_rules: Stop for unstable foot, discomfort or uncontrolled return.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable lateral shift and return both sides without forced depth.

competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

full.other_contact_accounting: Six bilateral landing events, six per foot: event count 6, foot-contact count 12.
full.prerequisite: Previously passed comfortable low bilateral rebound and stop; current total impact budget permits it.
full.count_definition: One bilateral rebound and landing is one event involving both feet; do not double the event count when summing feet.

count_reconciliation.calculation: 6 bilateral landing events × 2 feet = 12 landing foot contacts (6 each foot), not 12 rebound repetitions.
count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

records.name: Bodyweight hip hinge with reach — concluding check
records.purpose: Observe comfortable hip-dominant movement, foot pressure and trunk control before the two target drills.

card_mapping_status.limit: A loaded RDL is not the exact identity of this unloaded reach check. Exact current card/support/profile remains unverified.

records.setup: Three five-athlete waves A, B, C. Both coaches view active lane from front-oblique and side-oblique positions, dividing athletes 2/3. Other lanes stand and add no repetitions.
cues: Soften knees and send hips back.
Keep useful foot pressure and comfortable trunk position.
stop_rules: Stop for pain, balance loss or uncontrolled trunk; reduce range/use thigh support only when comfortable.

competency_rule.observe: Observe hip-back strategy and control; loaded-pattern assessment remains in strength.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.

stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

reviewable_modifications.reason: Keep purpose with no crossing or long queue travel.

reviewable_modifications.alternative_arithmetic: At 32 seconds per athlete, five serial waves in three parallel lanes require at least 160 seconds of work before demo/clearance, versus 32 seconds with separate bays: 128 seconds extra. Adding that to the complete full clock exceeds 720 seconds without another explicit change.

validation.count_accounting_status: PASS: all 192 age/profile dose objects have explicit primary count units; included numeric doses reconcile through segment primary-unit contributions; bilateral landings retain event/foot distinction; null unknown contact counts remain null; override routes resolve explicit dose/rest/profile references or explicit zero-dose omission.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
counting_conventions.segment_repetitions: Each execution segment has its own count_unit. Its duration remains repetitions × seconds_each. Primary count contributions convert the segment counts to the record primary unit; complete cycles remain the accepted unit.
counting_conventions.SP-09_and_fallback_normalization: A-March primary counts are now individual steps: 8 familiar (4 each side) or 4 OR (2 each side). Bilateral cycle counts are explicit secondary metadata; actual movement/time unchanged.
counting_conventions.SP-13_correction: Familiar full/compact is 16 individual ankling task contacts, eight each foot; OR01 full/compact is four individual foot-roll/replace actions, two each foot. No execution duration or physical dose changed.
counting_conventions.contact_rule: Landing events and per-foot landing contacts are separate. Timed jogging/actual ankling flight count stays null when not predetermined, never zero by default.
